ProvaLivre

A different, fair exam for every student, in one click.

Anti-cheating exams for public schools with limited resources

Carine Zambrano  •  MGT 409

The problem

My uncle Érick teaches Mechanics of Solids at a public technical high school in Brazil, a five-year program with limited resources.

  • Students copy each other during exams, called "filar"
  • The same exam gets reused, so answers pass down across years
  • Making a unique exam per student by hand is not feasible

"Each student's exam should pull random questions, same difficulty, different exam, so they cannot copy."

What is new

ToolGap for Érick
Canvas, Google ClassroomNo exam generation
Google Forms, QuizizzShuffle order only, same questions and numbers
ChatGPTNo bank, no guaranteed-correct math, no per-student assembly

ProvaLivre: per-student exams with numeric variants computed by code, built from the teacher's own material, with a human review step and worked solutions.

How the agents work

The model writes the questions once. Python computes the math. A free, deterministic assembler builds every student's exam.
